what: Crown Holdings makes metal cans: the aluminium cans that hold beer and soft drinks, food cans, aerosol cans, and the steel strapping used to secure freight.
customers: Brewers, soft drink bottlers, food canners and industrial shippers, on multi-year supply contracts.
money: aluminium beverage cans in North and South America
steel and plastic strapping and protective packaging
beverage and food cans in Asia
moat: Can plants are built next to the filling lines they supply, because shipping empty cans any distance is uneconomic. Once a plant is in place beside a brewery, nobody else can compete for that volume.
risks: Aluminium prices are passed through with a lag, so a spike squeezes the margin for a quarter or two
Beverage can volumes grow slowly and follow drinks consumption
opportunities: 16.5 times earnings and 12.7 times free cash flow with $1.0B of free cash flow
Revenue has recovered from $11.8B to $12.4B and the margin has improved
Cans are taking share from glass and plastic in drinks, helped by recycling rules
watch: Beverage can shipment volumes and the pass-through of aluminium costs.
